reason: A measurement of a positioned part: corolla lip (FLOPO_0985017) with position adaxial, plus length as a bounded measurement (pattern 02). Not a quality word.
rostrate is an exact synonym of FLOPO:0991028 beaked. 'long' only grades the beak and stays in the record as a qualifier.
A compound of sulcate (FLOPO:0991061) and angular (PATO_0001977), parallel to PATO striate-angular. Both values hold of the stem, so it needs no new term.
A comparison with another part: increased length (PATO_0000573) towards sepal (PO_0009031), as pattern 09 handles 'longer than'.
A poriform stigma or fig ostiole is reduced to a minute, point-like opening. PATO punctiform (small and resembling a point) is the nearest existing term.
A light preference of the habitat, not a quality of the plant's form. Unlike epiphytic or aquatic, it does not say where the plant is placed.
A lobe of the corolla, labellum or leaf with position lateral (FLOPO:0991380), plus a length measurement. A positioned part with a measure, not a quality.
strigillose / strigilleux / estrigiloso is the spelling variant of strigulose: minutely strigose.
A degree between approximate (FLOPO:0991190) and distant (FLOPO:0991189) with no definite value. Too vague for a term or a rule.
'Allomorphic flowers present' is a descriptor of one flora whose meaning (other-formed flowers in the inflorescence) is not standard. Mapping it to dimorphic (FLOPO:0991092) would be a guess.
'Berries palatable' means fit to eat: PATO edible (suitable for use as food). Taste such as 'sour' goes to FLOPO:0991340.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (surface or region of the bearer)
reason: A quality of a region of the bearer: base of the ovary, blade or achene plus decreased width (PATO_0000599).
Half-moon-shaped = lunate, a RELATED synonym of crescent-shaped. The earlier review mapped 'lunate' the same way (C314).
'Roots shoot-bearing' says the root bears shoots (root suckers): presence of a shoot axis arising from the root.
A compound of panicle-like (FLOPO:0991198) and raceme-like (FLOPO:0991197) inflorescence form. It needs no term of its own.
Two values of different attributes: triangular (PATO_0001875) shape and approximately peltate (FLOPO:0991107) attachment.
'Leaves in spirals' = leaves inserted singly along a spiral round the stem.
Brunnescent = brownish, becoming brown, used as a colour of midribs, testa and blades. The '-escent' degree stays in the record.
A labellum or corolla-lip lobe with position median (FLOPO:0991381), plus a length measurement. Not a quality.
A part, not a quality. Isocotylous = cotyledons equal, so cotyledon (PO_0020030) + equal (FLOPO:0991102).
States that a rhizome (PO_0004542) is present and short: the part rhizome with decreased length (PATO_0000574). It needs no compound term.
pitted maps to foveate (earlier review, C179). 'minutely' = foveolate, a RELATED synonym of foveate.
A compound of reticulate (FLOPO:0991100) and striated (PATO_0001410) on a pyrene, nutlet or stem surface.
A compound of two pilosity values, pubescent (PATO_0000455) and hispid (PATO_0002339). It belongs to the continuum pattern, not a term.
Negates bulbous (bulb-shaped) for trichomes and style bases.
Recaulescence = a bract or bracteole adnate to the axis above its node, so it is shifted up the peduncle. Model it as adnate (FLOPO:0991129) towards the axis.
bordered is an exact synonym of margined. 'narrowly' grades the border width and stays in the record.

target: leaf adaxial stomatal complex (PO_0025191) present and leaf abaxial stomatal complex (PO_0025190) present
reason: Amphistomatic = stomata on both leaf surfaces. PO has both surface-specific stomatal complexes, so two presence statements express it without a new term.

label: antrorsely barbellate
definition: A texture quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's surface bearing minute barbs that point forward, towards its apex. NOTE: FLOPO:0991087 barbellate is defined with backward-pointing barbs, so this cannot be its child. If barbellate is widened to 'minute barbs', move this under it with a retrorsely barbellate sibling.
reason: A standard character of pappus and perianth bristles (Cyperaceae, Asteraceae). Not covered by barbellate as FLOPO now defines it.
In wood and bark it describes the specimen's condition, and in fruit it is a vague texture word. PATO wet means covered by liquid, which is not meant here.
